verses.13:1a: Disse o {insipiens} no seu coração: * Não há Deus.
verses.13:1b: {corrupti}, e tornaram-se abomináveis nos seus {studiis}: * não há quem faça o bem, não há {usque1}.
verses.13:2: O Senhor {prospexit} os filhos dos homens, * para ver se há quem entenda, ou quem {requirens} a Deus.
verses.13:3a: Todos {declinaverunt}, {simul} se tornaram inúteis: * não há quem faça o bem, não há {usque3}.
verses.13:3b: A sua garganta é um sepulcro aberto, † com as suas línguas enganavam, * {venenum}.
verses.13:3c: A sua boca está cheia de maldição e de amargura: * {velozes} para derramar sangue.
verses.13:3d: {contritio} nos seus caminhos, † e não conheceram o caminho da paz: * não há temor de Deus diante dos seus olhos.
verses.13:4: {cognoscent} todos os que praticam a iniquidade, * os que devoram o meu povo {escam}?
verses.13:5: {invocaverunt}, * ali tremeram {timore}, onde não havia temor.
verses.13:6: Porque o Senhor está {generatione}, † {confudistis} o conselho do {inopis}: * porque o Senhor é a sua esperança.
verses.13:7: {quisdabit} de Sião a salvação de Israel? * quando o Senhor {averterit} do seu povo, {exsultabit}.

decisions.why: insípiens: 'unwise, foolish' (the Greek ἄφρων, 'senseless'). 13:1a = 52:1 word for word; the adjective also stands in 48:11 (simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt — beside stultus), 73:18 pópulus insípiens, 91:7 Vir insípiens non cognóscet: * et stultus non intélleget (beside stultus again), and the noun insipiéntia in 21:3, 37:6, 68:6 (grep). So the word must stay apart from stultus. Douay-Rheims 'The fool'; Matos Soares 1932 'O insensato' in Ps 13 but 'o néscio' in Ps 52 (his two twins differ); the Diurnal (from the Hebrew) 'O insensato'.

options.label: insensato
options.note: Ruling: the lack of sense (in-sípiens, ἄ-φρων) heard in the word itself; current, serious, and free for the noun (insipiéntia → insensatez); leaves 'tolo' / 'estulto' for stultus (48:11, 91:7). Matos Soares 1932 in this psalm, and the Diurnal's word. Ps 52:1 should copy it.

options.label: néscio
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 in Ps 52:1. Literary, and a proparoxytone.

options.label: tolo
options.note: Plain, but it is the natural word for stultus, which stands beside insípiens in 48:11 and 91:7.

decisions.why: A perfect passive with no agent; the Greek has the active διέφθειραν ('they have corrupted [their ways]'), and in Ps 52:2 the passive διεφθάρησαν. Douay-Rheims 'They are corrupt'; Matos Soares 1932 'corromperam-se'. The same words open 52:2.

options.label: Corromperam-se
options.note: Ruling: the medio-passive with the se, as Ps 8:2b 'se elevou' for eleváta est and Ps 11:2 'diminuíram' for diminútæ sunt; no agent is invented; Matos Soares 1932's wording. It pairs with 'tornaram-se' in the same colon. Ps 52:2 should copy it.

options.label: Estão corrompidos
options.note: The state (Douay-Rheims 'are corrupt'); the perfect's event is lost.

options.label: Foram corrompidos
options.note: The passive to the letter; it asks by whom.

decisions.why: Glossary: stúdia → feitos (open, Ps 9:12, where the Greek is ἐπιτηδεύματα, 'pursuits, practices'); its row names this verse as the one other place of the word to test it (grep: 9:12 and 13:1b only). Here the Greek is again ἐν ἐπιτηδεύμασιν. Douay-Rheims 'in their ways'; Matos Soares 1932 'nos seus desejos'. Ps 52:2 has in iniquitátibus instead, so the twin does not follow here.

options.label: feitos
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word (what one busies oneself doing), as in 9:12 'anunciai entre as nações os seus feitos' — there of God, here of the wicked; the word is neutral as stúdia is.

options.label: empenhos
options.note: Nearer to stúdium (zeal, application); in Brazil also a pawn or a commitment.

options.label: desejos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. 'Desejo' is desidérium's.

options.label: caminhos
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'ways'; 'caminho' is via's, and 13:3d has viis → 'caminhos'.

decisions.why: 'There is not, up to one' — none, not even one (οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός). The same second colon closes 13:1b and 13:3a, and 13:3a = 52:4 word for word; Romans 3:12 has it too (Clementine text fetched: consult/bolls-VULG-45-3.json). Douay-Rheims 'no not one'; Matos Soares 1932 'não há nem sequer um' (13), 'não há sequer um só' (52).

options.label: nem sequer um
options.note: Ruling: the idiom Portuguese has for 'not even one', and the colon ends on the stressed 'um' as the Latin ends on 'unum'. The same in both verses; Ps 52:4 copies 13:3a.

options.label: nem um só
options.note: Also plain; 'só' adds an idea.

options.label: até um
options.note: The Latin to the letter; not Portuguese in this sense.

decisions.latin: Dóminus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum
decisions.why: prospícere: 'to look forward, into the distance, to look out' (Lewis & Short); the Greek διέκυψεν 'leaned out and looked down'. The verb recurs 84:12 justítia de cælo prospéxit, 101:20 prospéxit de excélso sancto suo, and the twin 52:3 (with Deus); it must stay apart from respícere (Ps 10:5b 'estar voltado para', 12:3 'olhai') and aspícere (118:132 'Olhai para mim'). super → sobre (glossary, place). Douay-Rheims 'hath looked down from heaven upon'; Matos Soares 1932 'olhou do céu para' (13), 'olhou do céu sobre' (52). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «olhou sobre» soa transportada do latim; a boca espera «olhou para» — and he proposed the whole verse with ‘Do céu, o Senhor olhou para …’. The Latinist passed ‘sobre’.

options.label: olhou do céu para
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the preposition Portuguese gives ‘olhar’ (Matos Soares 1932 in this psalm, and the stylist). A preposition follows the verb it hangs on — grammar (D2); what super adds, the look coming down, is still said by ‘do céu’. The stylist’s fronting (‘Do céu, o Senhor olhou para’) was not taken: the Latin’s order is also good Portuguese. Ps 52:3 should copy it (with Deus).

options.label: olhou do céu sobre
options.note: Draft 1. the plain verb of seeing, and 'sobre' for super, which keeps the look coming down from above as 'de cælo … super' does. Matos Soares 1932 in Ps 52:3. The 'pro-' (looking out, into the distance) is not heard: no plain Portuguese verb has it.

options.label: se debruçou do céu sobre
options.note: The Greek's image (διακύπτω, to lean out); vivid, but it is the Greek's, not the Latin's verb.

decisions.why: requírere: the glossary has quǽrere → buscar and exquírere → procurar, and merged requírere into procurar at 118:145 because the Greek there is ἐκζητέω, the verb behind exquírere. Here the Greek is again ἐκζητῶν. So by the same test the verb is 'procurar'. (9:13 requírens sánguinem, of God, is 'pedir contas', another sense.) 13:2b = 52:3b word for word, and Romans 3:11 has 'non est requirens Deum' (Clementine, fetched). Douay-Rheims 'seek God'; Matos Soares 1932 'busque a Deus'; the Diurnal 'busca a Deus'.

options.label: procure
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb for the Greek ἐκζητέω (exquírere, and requírere at 118:145); 'procurar a Deus' is current Portuguese. Ps 52:3 should copy it.

options.label: busque
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal: the familiar line ('quem busque a Deus'), but 'buscar' is quǽrere's, which the glossary keeps apart from exquírere.

decisions.why: declináre (ἐξέκλιναν, 'turned aside'), here absolute. The glossary row 'declináre a → apartar-se de' (open, Ps 118:21 …) is for the build with a; it keeps 'desviar' for avértere (transitive: 'Desviai os males', 53:7; 'desviais … a vossa face', 12:1). 13:3a = 52:4 = Romans 3:12 (fetched). Douay-Rheims 'They are all gone aside'; Matos Soares 1932 'Todos se extraviaram' ('extraviar-se' is erráre's in the glossary, 118:110).

options.label: se desviaram
options.note: Ruling: the plain Portuguese for turning aside from the way, which is the Latin's sense. The reflexive 'desviar-se' is not avértere's transitive 'desviar' (avértere is never absolute in the psalter — grep: 13:7, 77:38, 77:57 avertérunt se, 105:24), though one of those, 77:57 avertérunt se, will want 'se desviaram' too — so the two Latin verbs will share a Portuguese form there. Chosen over 'apartar-se' because with 'juntos' in the same colon 'Todos se apartaram, juntos …' can be heard as 'they separated from one another' — to be tested on the blind reader. Ps 52:4 copies it.

options.label: se apartaram
options.note: The glossary's verb for declináre a. Absolute, and next to 'juntos', it can be heard as parting from each other.

options.label: se extraviaram
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. 'Extraviar-se' is erráre's (glossary, 118:110).

decisions.why: simul (ἅμα): 'together, at the same time'. 15 lines in the psalter (grep), most of them 'together' (30:14 convenírent simul, 87:18 circumdedérunt me simul), some 'alike' (48:11 simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt). The glossary gives 'juntos' to in unum (2:2, open), and 48:3 has simul in unum. Douay-Rheims 'together'; Matos Soares 1932 'todos' (13), 'juntamente' (52). inútiles facti sunt → 'se tornaram inúteis' (ἠχρεώθησαν, 'became worthless'); facti sunt as in 13:1b.

options.label: juntos
options.note: Ruling: the plain word, Douay-Rheims' 'together'. It shares 'juntos' with in unum (glossary, open); where the two meet (48:3 simul in unum) that verse decides.

options.label: juntamente
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (Ps 52): one word of its own for simul, heavier.

options.label: ao mesmo tempo
options.note: The temporal sense; three syllables longer.

decisions.why: The third colon has no verb in the Latin, the Greek (ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν) or Romans 3:13 (fetched). The first two colons are Ps 5:11a's word for word and are copied from it ('A sua garganta é um sepulcro aberto, † com as suas línguas enganavam'), as the glossary's formula row asks; Ps 5 left its own second colon verbless as DO points it. sub → 'debaixo de' (glossary: sub pédibus → debaixo dos pés, 8:8). Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal 'debaixo dos seus lábios há veneno de áspides'.

options.label: veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios

forms.venenum: veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios

options.note: Ruling: verbless, as the Latin; a third item in the list of what their mouths hold, and the colon ends on the lips as the Latin's does.

options.label: há veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios

forms.venenum: há veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios

options.note: The verb supplied (D2 allows it); one syllable more.

options.label: debaixo dos seus lábios há veneno de áspides

forms.venenum: debaixo dos seus lábios há veneno de áspides

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal; ends on the proparoxytone 'áspides'.

decisions.latin: Contrítio et infelícitas in viis eórum
decisions.why: contrítio (σύντριμμα): a crushing, a breaking — the noun of contérere (glossary: → quebrar, open). The noun recurs only as contritiónes (59:4 sana contritiónes ejus; 146:3 álligat contritiónes eórum — the breaches of the land, the wounds of the broken-hearted; grep). infelícitas (ταλαιπωρία, 'misery'): only here. The colon is verbless in the Latin, as in Romans 3:16 (fetched). Douay-Rheims 'Destruction and unhappiness'; Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal 'aflição e desgraça'. 'Destruição' is proposed for intéritus (9:16a); 'quebranto' in Brazil is the evil eye.

options.label: Ruína e infelicidade
options.note: Ruling: 'ruína' is the concrete wreck of a thing broken, as σύντριμμα is; 'infelicidade' is the cognate, current and plain. Verbless, as the Latin. Cost: ruína is also a Latin word of the psalter (105:29, 109:6, 143:14, grep), which will want another Portuguese there or share this one.

options.label: Destruição e infelicidade
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'Destruction'; the glossary proposes 'destruição' for intéritus.

options.label: Quebranto e infelicidade
options.note: Of the family of 'quebrar' (contérere); refused: in Brazil 'quebranto' is the evil eye.

options.label: Aflição e desgraça
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (and the Diurnal). 'Aflição' names a feeling where the Latin names a breaking.

decisions.why: A question expecting 'yes' (nonne), future (οὐχὶ γνώσονται), with no object: shall they not come to know? cognóscere → conhecer (glossary), but 'conhecer' without an object is not Portuguese; the glossary already lets conhecer / saber follow Portuguese collocation (118:125, 118:152 'soube'). 13:3d cognovérunt (with an object, viam) keeps 'conheceram'. The twin 52:5 has scient (the same Greek γνώσονται). Douay-Rheims 'Shall not all they know'; Matos Soares 1932 'Porventura não terão conhecimento' (13), 'não se lembrarão' (52, his gloss).

options.label: Não hão de saber
options.note: Ruling: the future of a question that expects 'yes' — 'hão de' is the Portuguese form for what is bound to come (cf. Ps 12:2 'hei de pôr'); 'saber' because 'conhecer' needs an object. Ps 52:5 (scient, same Greek) should copy it.

options.label: Não saberão
options.note: The simple future; heard as a statement until the question mark comes, at the end of the verse.

options.label: Não conhecerão
options.note: The glossary verb; no object follows, so the ear waits for one.

options.label: Porventura não terão conhecimento
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: a noun for the verb, and long.

decisions.latin: qui dévorant plebem meam sicut escam panis
decisions.why: 'As a meal of bread' (βρώσει ἄρτου, the eating of bread): they eat up the people as one eats bread. 52:5 has ut cibum panis — the Latin varies the noun, the Greek has βρώσει ἄρτου both times, so by D15's test the two can share a rendering. plebs → povo (glossary, open). Douay-Rheims 'as they eat bread'; Matos Soares 1932 'como um pedaço de pão' (13), 'como quem come pão' (52). The Latinist (draft 2, minor) read esca as the food and asked for ‘como alimento de pão’; kept as an option.

options.label: como quem come pão
options.note: Ruling: the eating (esca, βρῶσις) and the bread both heard, in the plainest Portuguese; Matos Soares 1932 in Ps 52:5. Ps 52:5 (ut cibum panis, the same Greek) should copy it.

options.label: como comida de pão
options.note: The noun kept; not said so in Portuguese.

options.label: como se come o pão
options.note: Impersonal; also plain.

options.label: como alimento de pão
options.note: The Latinist (draft 2, minor; he passed the ruling on draft 1): the Latin compares the people to bread as food, not the devourers to one who eats. Refused: esca here is the Greek βρώσει, the act of eating (Douay-Rheims ‘as they eat bread’), and ‘alimento de pão’ is not said in Portuguese.

decisions.latin: illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor
decisions.why: timor → temor (glossary). The Latin says the noun twice (timóre … timor; the Greek φόβῳ … φόβος), and the second colon is the same in 52:6. trepidáre: 'to tremble, be agitated with fear' (only here and 52:6, grep). Douay-Rheims 'trembled for fear, where there was no fear'; Matos Soares 1932 'tremeram de medo, onde não havia que tremer'.

options.label: de temor
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's noun, said twice as the Latin says it (rule 2); 'tremer de temor' is less usual than 'tremer de medo' but plain. Ps 52:6 copies the colon.

options.label: de medo
options.note: The idiom (Matos Soares 1932); the repetition timóre … timor is lost, and 'medo' is not the glossary's word.

decisions.latin: Quóniam Dóminus in generatióne justa est
decisions.why: 'For the Lord is in the just generation' (ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἐν γενεᾷ δικαίᾳ). Douay-Rheims 'in the just generation'; Matos Soares 1932 'está com a geração dos justos' (explains 'in' as 'with'). Ps 52 has another verse here (52:6b Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa …), so nothing is shared.

options.label: na geração justa
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's preposition and adjective; the Lord is among, in, the just generation.

options.label: com a geração dos justos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: 'with' for 'in', and the adjective turned into a noun.

decisions.why: The psalmist turns to the evildoers, plural (confudístis, κατῃσχύνατε), between two verses that speak of the Lord in the third person. confúndi → ser envergonhado, active 'envergonhar' (glossary, settled D15). consílium → conselho (glossary). A cost of vós: God is vós in this psalter, and Ps 10:2's blind reader heard a bare plural 'dizeis' first as said to the Lord; the remedy there was to name the subject, 'como dizeis vós', against 'o Senhor' — used here too. Douay-Rheims 'you have confounded the counsel of the poor man'; Matos Soares 1932 'Vós (ó ímpios) escarnecestes do projecto do infeliz' (his gloss names the addressees).

options.label: vós envergonhastes
options.note: Ruling: the settled verb (D15), active; the subject named (grammar, D2) so that the ear takes a new addressee, set between two 'o Senhor'. To be tested on the blind reader: whether it is heard as said to God.

options.label: envergonhastes
options.note: Bare, as the Latin; Ps 10:2 shows the risk of a bare vós form beside God.

options.label: vós confundistes
options.note: The cognate; D15 moved confúndi to 'envergonhar' because 'confundir' is heard as 'to muddle'.

options.label: vós frustrastes
options.note: What putting a plan to shame amounts to; it explains.

decisions.why: Glossary: inops → indigente (open; D27 left it open because the blind reader of Ps 11 listed 'indigentes' as unknown twice), pauper → pobre. The row names 13:6 among inops's 14 lines. Here the psalm has no pauper, so nothing forces a distinction inside the verse. Douay-Rheims 'the poor man'; Matos Soares 1932 'do infeliz'. The next colon's 'ejus' (a sua esperança) points back to this man. Draft 3: D38 rules inops → “carente”; “indigente” and “desvalido” stay options.

options.label: carente
options.note: Draft 3, ruled by the main session (D38; review of the finished work, 2026-09-21). “Indigente” was unknown to four blind readers out of four; “carente” passed (Ps 34:10b). One word for inops through the psalter. “O conselho do carente” keeps “conselho”: D33 leaves conselho where a verse can mean both (review/consistency.md 1.2). No critic has read draft 3.

options.label: indigente
options.note: Drafts 1–2, the then-working row (inops → indigente). the glossary's working word, so that inops is one word through the psalter and a third test is had on a blind reader.

options.label: pobre
options.note: The plain word (Douay-Rheims 'poor man'); it is pauper's.

options.label: desvalido
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's word for inops in Ps 11:6a.

decisions.latin: Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël?
decisions.why: 'Who will give …?' is also the Latin (and Greek, τίς δώσει) idiom for a wish ('O that …!'), as in 54:7 Quis dabit mihi pennas. The Latin leaves the question and the wish together; DO prints '?'. 13:7a = 52:7a word for word. salutáre → salvação (D6). Douay-Rheims 'Who shall give out of Sion'; Matos Soares 1932 'Quem enviará'.

options.label: Quem dará
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb and its question; the wish is heard through it, as it is in the Latin. Ps 52:7 copies the colon.

options.label: Quem enviará
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: another verb.

options.label: Oxalá venha
options.note: The wish alone (the Diurnal's 'Venha', from the Hebrew's sense); closes what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.latin: cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ
decisions.why: 'When the Lord shall have turned away the captivity of his people' (ἐν τῷ ἐπιστρέψαι κύριον τὴν αἰχμαλωσίαν). Here the twins part: 52:7 has cum convérterit Deus — one Greek verb, two Latin verbs — and 84:2 avertísti captivitátem Jacob has this one; 125:1, 125:4 have convértere (grep). Glossary: avértere → desviar (open; 'Desviai os males', 'desviais a vossa face'), convértere → voltar. Future perfect → Portuguese future subjunctive. Douay-Rheims 'shall have turned away the captivity'; Matos Soares 1932 'puser fim ao cativeiro'. Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «“Desviar o cativeiro” soa pouco português» → ‘afastar’. The blind reader took ‘desviar o cativeiro’ first as ‘afastar ou evitar o cativeiro; o verbo não deixa evidente se ele já está acontecendo’ — which is as open as ‘turn away’ is in the Latin; the second hearing, averting a captivity still to come, is also a hearing of avértere.

options.label: afastar o cativeiro
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s verb. ‘Afastar’ is ‘turn away / put away’ in plain Portuguese, and says avértere’s image without the unidiomatic ‘desviar’ (which stays right for avértere with a face or with anger, 12:1, 77:38, 105:24). Cost: ‘afastar’ is the glossary’s working verb for amovére / repéllere (open) — they never stand in a verse with captivitátem (grep); 84:2 avertísti captivitátem Jacob should follow this psalm (‘afastastes o cativeiro de Jacó’). The blind reader’s doubt (a captivity present or threatened) stays, as in the Latin.

options.label: desviar o cativeiro
options.note: Draft 1. the glossary's verb for avértere, so that 13:7 and 84:2 say one thing and 52:7 (convértere → 'fizer voltar') can differ as the Latin does. 'Desviar o cativeiro' is unusual, but it says 'turn away' — which is the Latin's image — and the second half of the verse shows what it means. To be tested on the blind reader.

options.label: puser fim ao cativeiro
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense; it explains the image.

decisions.latin: velóces pedes eórum ad effundéndum sánguinem
decisions.why: A verbless clause in the Latin (and in Romans 3:15, fetched): ‘swift their feet to shed blood’. Portuguese supplies ‘são’. Draft 1 kept the adjective first, as the Latin; the stylist: «A inversão dá à frase um tom declamatório que destoa da simplicidade do primeiro membro».

options.label: os seus pés são velozes
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s order — order yields to the ear (D2); every word kept. Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal build it so (‘os seus pés são ligeiros’).

options.label: velozes são os seus pés
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s order, adjective first; heard by the stylist as declamatory.

decisions.why: Draft 1 ‘Não invocaram o Senhor, * … onde não havia temor’ rhymed at mediant and final (Senhor / temor, flagged by checks.py and by the stylist: «“Senhor” na mediana rima com “temor” no final … A repetição de “temor” pertence ao texto e deve ficar»). The Latin has no such rhyme (invocavérunt / timor). The Latin puts the object first; 52:6a has the same words with Deum.

options.label: Ao Senhor não invocaram
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s line — which is the Latin’s own order, object first; the fronted object takes ‘a’ as Portuguese does with a fronted name of God. The rhyme goes, the colon ends on a paroxytone. Ps 52:6a should copy it: ‘A Deus não invocaram’.

options.label: Não invocaram o Senhor
options.note: Draft 1: natural order; rhymes with the final ‘temor’.

decisions.why: The last colon is the longest of the psalm (31 Latin syllables). The stylist («o membro também exige um fôlego longo; a ordem direta alivia a dicção») proposed the direct order. The words are 52:7’s too.

options.label: Jacó exultará, e Israel se alegrará

forms.exsultabit: Jacó exultará, e Israel se alegrará

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): subject before verb, as the stylist asked — order only (D2); the verse now ends on the verb ‘alegrará’, not on a second ‘Israel’ (draft 1 ended both colons on ‘Israel’, the Latin’s own echo, flagged as a rhyme). Ps 52:7 copies it.

options.label: exultará Jacó, e se alegrará Israel

forms.exsultabit: exultará Jacó, e se alegrará Israel

options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s order, verb first; both colons end on ‘Israel’, as the Latin’s do.

choices.13:1a: The psalm begins at 13:1a (the titulus In finem, Psalmus David is out, D7). 13:1a = 52:1 word for word. 'Não há Deus' as 9:26a has it ('Não há Deus à vista dele').
choices.13:1b: facti sunt → 'tornaram-se', and again in 13:3a (the Latin's repetition kept; the glossary's fíeri row keeps 'fazer-se' for Ps 117 and allows 'tornar-se' for a state that comes upon one, 118:83). 'Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt' and 'non est qui fáciat bonum' are 52:2's words too; its middle (in iniquitátibus) and its end (no usque ad unum) differ.
choices.13:2: 13:2 differs from 52:3 in one word only: Dóminus / Deus. intéllegens → 'quem entenda' (intellégere → entender, glossary). fílii hóminum → 'filhos dos homens' (glossary).
choices.13:3a: 13:3a = 52:4 word for word, and = Romans 3:12 (Clementine text fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-45-3.json).
choices.13:3b: 13:3b–3d are not in the Hebrew (WLC, consult/parallels/ps013.md) nor in Ps 52; they are in the Rahlfs Septuagint text on disk (its verse 3) and in the Clementine Vulgate (bolls-VULG-19-13.json, verse 3), and they stand word for word in Romans 3:13–18 (bolls-VULG-45-3.json). How they came into the Greek psalm is not verified here and is not asserted. The first two colons copy Ps 5:11a exactly (glossary formula; dolóse agébant → 'enganavam', the light verb yields as in Ps 5).
choices.13:3c: Quorum (a relative running on from 13:3b) → ‘A sua boca’, a new sentence: Portuguese does not open a prayed verse with ‘Cuja’; grammar (D2). maledíctio → maldição, amaritúdo → amargura. ‘são’ supplied in the second colon (decision velozes). effúndere → derramar (the glossary reserves ‘derramar’ for it, row eructáre).
choices.13:3d: via → caminho (both 'in viis' and 'viam pacis'). ante óculos eórum → 'diante dos seus olhos' (as ante óculos tuos in Ps 5). cognovérunt with an object keeps 'conheceram'.
choices.13:4: operári iniquitátem → 'praticar a iniquidade' (glossary). plebs → povo (glossary, open; its row names 13:7). The colon 'todos os que praticam a iniquidade, * os que devoram o meu povo' is shared with 52:5 word for word.
choices.13:5: 13:5b = 52:6b word for word. invocáre → invocar (glossary). Draft 1’s rhyme Senhor / temor removed by the Latin’s own order (decision invocaverunt).
choices.13:6: spes → esperança. The Latin's two quóniam kept as two 'porque'.
choices.13:7: Jacob → Jacó (the Brazilian form). exsultáre / lætári → exultar / alegrar-se (glossary). 13:7a and the last clause (captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Jacob, et lætábitur Israël) are 52:7's words too.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm13.txt, eleven prayed verses with DO's ids (13:1a, 1b, 2, 3a, 3b, 3c, 3d, 4, 5, 6, 7). Collated against the Clementine Vulgate fetched from Bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-19-13.json): no difference of wording (Sepúlcrum / Sepulchrum is spelling). The Clementine prints 13:3b–3d inside its verse 3; the Rahlfs LXX on disk has them in verse 3 too; the Hebrew (WLC) has no such lines. Romans 3:10–18 fetched (consult/bolls-VULG-45-3.json): 3:12 = 13:3a, 3:13–18 = 13:3b–3d, word for word.

Ps 13 and Ps 52 side by side (consult/parallels/ps052.md; bolls-VULG-19-52.json). Shared word for word: 13:1a = 52:1; 13:3a = 52:4; 13:5b = 52:6b (illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor); 13:7a = 52:7a (Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël?); and the end of 13:7 (captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Jacob, et lætábitur Israël). Shared in part: 13:1b / 52:2 (Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt … non est qui fáciat bonum — 52 has in iniquitátibus, and no second colon member); 13:2 / 52:3 (Dóminus / Deus only); 13:4 / 52:5 (cognóscent / scient, sicut escam / ut cibum — one Greek each time); 13:5a / 52:6a (Dóminum / Deum). Not shared: 13:3b–3d (not in 52); 13:6 against 52:6b (Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa …); cum avérterit Dóminus / cum convérterit Deus (13:7). Ps 52 is not yet translated: this psalm writes the shared words so that it can copy them (glossary, Doublets).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps013.md. Sense from the Vulgate family (Douay-Rheims; Matos Soares 1932 by its text layer, his parenthetical glosses ignored). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 has the psalm, from the Hebrew: diction only; its sense refused where it follows the Hebrew (13:5–6 'pois o Senhor os dispersou … Secaram os ossos do ímpio' is the Hebrew / Ps 52's verse, not this Latin's). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Lewis & Short read for prospicio. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: insípiens (14 lines), declinavérunt (5), simul (15), prospéxit (5), requírens (3), contrítio (3), escam (17), captivitátem (7), avértere (4). Glossary applied: insensato (new), feitos (stúdia, open — its test), procurar (requírere = ἐκζητέω), praticar a iniquidade, envergonhar (confúndere, D15), indigente (inops, open — a third test), desviar (avértere, open), salvação (D6), povo (plebs), temor. Decisions: 17.

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 13:3b first colon +3 (the Ps 5:11a formula, copied as the glossary asks); 13:3c second colon −3; 13:6 −3 / +4 / +3 (the named subject ‘vós’ and ‘indigente’; the Latin colons are short). Rhyme flags: 13:5 Senhor / temor — a real accidental rhyme, sent to the critics; 13:7 Israel / Israel — the Latin’s own echo (Israël / Israël), rule 5’s exception.

Draft 1. Clean: no remark on any verse; the marks confirmed. Passed in particular ‘Corromperam-se’, ‘nos seus feitos’, ‘olhou do céu sobre’, ‘quem procure a Deus’, ‘Todos se desviaram’, the verbless ‘veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios’ and ‘Ruína e infelicidade nos seus caminhos’, ‘Não hão de saber’, ‘vós envergonhastes’, ‘desviar o cativeiro’.

Draft 1. Four verses; best 13:3a, worst 13:7. «O salmo tem austeridade e força oral, sobretudo nas repetições e nas imagens corporais … os principais tropeços vêm de algumas construções calcadas no latim e do longo membro final.» All four taken — each changes only how the thing is said (D2).

outcomes.remark: «olhou sobre» soa transportada do latim → ‘Do céu, o Senhor olhou para os filhos dos homens’
outcomes.reason: The preposition taken (‘para’, Matos Soares 1932’s); his fronting of ‘Do céu’ not taken — the Latin’s order is good Portuguese. ‘sobre’ is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘velozes são os seus pés’: the inversion is declamatory → ‘os seus pés são velozes’
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2). Draft 1’s order is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘Senhor’ at the mediant rhymes with ‘temor’ at the end → ‘Ao Senhor não invocaram’
outcomes.reason: His line is the Latin’s own order (Dóminum non invocavérunt) and removes a rhyme the Latin does not have; the repetition timóre … timor untouched, as he asked.

outcomes.remark: «Desviar o cativeiro» soa pouco português; the long colon wants the direct order → ‘afastar o cativeiro … Jacó exultará e Israel se alegrará’
outcomes.reason: ‘afastar’ says avértere’s image in plain Portuguese (the glossary’s ‘desviar’ holds for a face or anger, not for a captivity); the direct order (decision exsultabit) is order only and ends the verse on the verb instead of a second ‘Israel’.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 22 items, 4 unknown words (áspides, iniquidade, indigente, exultará). No wrong first hearing that the Latin excludes. Tests passed: ‘Todos se desviaram’ heard as turning from the good (not as parting); ‘vós envergonhastes’ heard as said to the evildoers (the Ps 10:2 remedy holds here); ‘Não hão de saber’ heard as ‘they will come to know’ — the Latin’s nonne. ‘desviar o cativeiro’ heard as ‘afastar ou evitar’, present or threatened — the Latin’s range, but the stylist’s verb was taken anyway. ‘indigente’ listed as unknown for the third time (Pss 11 ×2, 13).

outcomes.remark: plural subject after the singular ‘insensato’: the fools / mankind
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s plural (corrúpti sunt) after its singular (insípiens); left as open as the Latin.

outcomes.remark: ‘os filhos dos homens’: mankind (heard first) / male descendants
outcomes.reason: Glossary; heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘quem entenda’: understanding in general / understanding God (heard first)
outcomes.reason: intéllegens has no object in the Latin either.

outcomes.remark: ‘Todos se desviaram’: all people turned from the good (heard first) / the wicked just named
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; the test of ‘desviar-se’ against ‘apartar-se’ next to ‘juntos’ passed.

outcomes.remark: whose throat, tongues and lips: the wicked (heard first) / all mankind
outcomes.reason: eórum is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘sepulcro aberto’: rot / speech that kills
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image, not explained.

outcomes.remark: ‘cheia de maldição e de amargura’: they utter curses (heard first) / they are cursed and bitter
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘Ruína e infelicidade nos seus caminhos’: they cause it (heard first) / they meet it
outcomes.reason: The Latin is open in the same way (in viis eórum).

outcomes.remark: ‘temor de Deus’: reverence (heard first) / fear of punishment
outcomes.reason: timor holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘Não hão de saber’: don’t they know? / they will come to know (heard first); no object
outcomes.reason: A question expecting ‘yes’ is heard as ‘they will know’: the Latin’s nonne cognóscent. No object in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: ‘o meu povo’: God speaking, unannounced (heard first) / the psalmist’s people
outcomes.reason: The Latin changes speaker the same way.

outcomes.remark: who did not invoke: the evildoers (heard first) / the people devoured
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘ali’: where they devoured / unnamed
outcomes.reason: illic is as unplaced.

outcomes.remark: ‘onde não havia temor’: no cause to fear (heard first) / no fear before / no reverence
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s repeated noun, open the same way.

outcomes.remark: ‘Porque …’ explains the trembling (heard first) or what follows
outcomes.reason: quóniam hangs the same way.

outcomes.remark: ‘na geração justa’: among the just / a just age (heard first)
outcomes.reason: generátio holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘vós envergonhastes’: the evildoers addressed (heard first) / the hearers
outcomes.reason: The test of the named subject passed: not heard as said to God.

outcomes.remark: ‘o conselho do indigente’: advice he gave (heard first) / his plan
outcomes.reason: consílium → conselho (glossary: open between advice and deliberation, as the Latin).

outcomes.remark: ‘a sua esperança’: the indigent’s (heard first) / the just generation’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘Quem dará de Sião’: who will bring salvation from Sion (heard first) / who in Sion will give
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘desviar o cativeiro’: end a present captivity / avert a threatened one (heard first: unclear)
outcomes.reason: The verb changed for the stylist’s sake (‘afastar’); the doubt present / threatened is the Latin’s own and stays.

outcomes.remark: ‘Jacó … Israel’: the people / a person and a country / one person
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s names, as they stand.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: áspides
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s snake named (rule 5); ‘cobras’ would lose the kind.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: iniquidade
outcomes.reason: Glossary (iníquitas → iniquidade).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: indigente
outcomes.reason: Kept under the glossary’s working rendering; the third ‘unknown’ is recorded in the row for the ruling.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: exultará
outcomes.reason: Glossary (exsultáre → exultar).

audit.note: v2. Four verses changed against draft 1, all from the stylist and each order or construction only: 13:2 ‘olhou do céu para’ (was ‘sobre’); 13:3c ‘os seus pés são velozes’ (was ‘velozes são’); 13:5 ‘Ao Senhor não invocaram’ (the Latin’s order; removes the rhyme Senhor / temor); 13:7 ‘afastar o cativeiro’ (was ‘desviar’) and ‘Jacó exultará, e Israel se alegrará’ (was verb first). Nothing held against the Latinist (he had no remark). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read).
Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as draft 1 (13:3b +3, 13:3c −3, 13:6 −3 / +4 / +3); the two rhyme flags are gone (13:5 by the Latin’s order; 13:7 now ends on ‘alegrará’).

Draft 2 — the gate. Clean of majors: one minor, 13:4, on words he passed unchanged on draft 1 — refused, his wording an option. Everything changed in draft 2 (13:2 ‘para’, 13:3c order, 13:5 ‘Ao Senhor não invocaram’, 13:7 ‘afastar o cativeiro’ and the order of the last clause) passed.

outcomes.remark: ‘como quem come pão’ compares the devourers to an eater; the Latin compares the people to bread as food → ‘como alimento de pão’ (minor)
outcomes.reason: esca is the Greek βρώσει, the eating (Douay-Rheims ‘as they eat bread’); his wording is not Portuguese; he passed the same words on draft 1 (D24: weighed).

audit.note: v3, by the main session, applying the review of the finished work (DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-21): 13:6 ínopis, “do indigente” → “do carente” (D38). No critic has read draft 3 — these verses are unread. Every earlier wording stays selectable.

Final gate on draft 3 (the D38 edit, “carente” at 13:6, had not been read). No major; “carente” clean. Two minors, both repeats or wordings already weighed; none taken, both live as options. Reader: claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context, with latin.json), run by the coordinator.

outcomes.remark: minor: “como quem come pão” moves the simile to the eater → “como alimento de pão”
outcomes.reason: The second time (v2 minor): esca is the Greek βρώσει, the eating (Douay-Rheims “as they eat bread”), and “alimento de pão” is not said in Portuguese. It is option 4.

outcomes.remark: minor: the explicit “vós” invites hearing the line as said to God → “envergonhastes”
outcomes.reason: The named subject was put there as a test and the blind reader passed it: it was not heard as said to God. The bare verb, which Ps 10:2 showed to be the riskier form, is option 2.
